{"slug": "ai-website-builder-vs-traditional-website-builder", "title": "AI Website Builder vs Traditional Website Builder", "metaTitle": "AI Website Builder vs Traditional Website Builder (2026 Guide)", "metaDescription": "AI website builders generate real code from a chat description. Traditional builders like Wix and WordPress use drag-and-drop editors. Here's the real difference, compared.", "targetKeyword": "ai website builder vs traditional website builder", "category": "Glossary", "bodyHtml": "

What each term actually means

An AI website builder is a tool where you describe the site you want in plain English, and the tool generates real source code — actual component files — behind the scenes. A traditional website builder (Wix, Squarespace, WordPress page builders like Elementor) is a visual, drag-and-drop editor: you place blocks, pick a template, and adjust settings inside a proprietary system that renders the page for you. Neither term is marketing fluff — they describe genuinely different production methods, and the difference shows up the moment you try to do something the tool wasn't designed for.

How each one actually works

Traditional website builders

You start from a template or a blank canvas, then drag sections, text blocks, images, and buttons into place. The builder stores your design as data inside its own platform — there's no file you can open in a code editor, because there isn't really a codebase in the conventional sense. Changes happen by clicking and dragging, not describing. This is why these tools have historically been the easiest entry point for non-technical users: what you see in the editor is what visitors see, with no code involved anywhere.

AI website builders

You type what you want — for example, a landing page for a bakery with a menu and a contact form — and the tool writes and compiles an actual application. Kodely, for instance, generates a real Vite + React 19 + TypeScript + Tailwind CSS v4 app: genuine .tsx component files, not a template with fields filled in. A live preview shows the compiled app as it's built. To change something, you describe the change in chat and the AI edits the real components, the same way a developer would, just faster. Because it's real code, you can open the code view and read the actual files it produced.

Side-by-side comparison

DimensionTraditional Website BuilderAI Website Builder
Output typeProprietary platform data rendered by the builder; no equivalent source filesReal, compiled source code — Kodely produces an actual Vite + React + TypeScript + Tailwind project
Editing modelDrag-and-drop blocks, templates, and settings panelsDescribe changes in chat; the AI edits the real components
Learning curveLow for basic layouts; steeper for custom design within the platform's constraintsLow to start with plain-English prompts; fine-grained visual control is more limited since there's no click-to-edit yet
Code accessNone — the design lives inside the platform, not as files you can openFull read access to generated files in-app (Kodely has a code view; no zip export yet)
HostingHosted on the platform, typically with custom domain support included or as a paid add-onVaries by tool; Kodely publishes free to a *.kodely.site URL, with no custom domains yet

Where traditional builders genuinely win

  • Massive template libraries covering almost any industry, refined over more than a decade.
  • Mature e-commerce stacks — inventory, shipping, tax, checkout — that have processed billions in transactions.
  • Huge plugin and app ecosystems, especially WordPress, for booking, membership, forms, and SEO.
  • Custom domains, email, and enterprise support are standard and well-documented.
  • Years of uptime and stability at massive scale — this is not new infrastructure.

Where AI builders genuinely win

  • Speed: describing a page in a sentence is faster than assembling it block by block, especially for a first draft.
  • No fighting the grid: you're not constrained to what a drag-and-drop layout engine can do, since the AI writes layout code directly.
  • Real, readable output: the code view shows actual source files, not a black-box render.
  • Iteration by conversation: asking to darken the hero section and move the pricing table up is a chat message, not a settings hunt.
  • Checkpoints: every successful generation is a free restore point, so experimenting doesn't risk losing a working version.

Who should pick which

If you need e-commerce with complex inventory, a large content site with years of plugins to lean on, or you want to hand a non-technical team member full visual control forever, a traditional builder is still the safer, more complete choice today. If you're prototyping fast, want a real codebase you can eventually hand to a developer, or you'd rather describe changes than click through menus, an AI builder like Kodely fits better. They're not strict replacements for each other yet — pick based on what you're actually building.

Where Kodely fits, honestly

Kodely is an AI website builder, not a traditional one, and it's currently frontend-only. It generates real Vite + React + TypeScript + Tailwind sites from a chat description, with a live preview, an in-app code view, and free checkpoints on every successful generation. Publishing is one click to a free *.kodely.site URL. Credits are metered from real AI cost, and a build that fails to compile is never charged; new accounts get 750 free credits with no card required, and every publish is scanned for leaked secrets before it goes live. What it doesn't do yet: no backend, database, auth, or payments generation, no custom domains, no code export as a zip, and no click-to-edit visual editing — only chat-based editing exists today. If your project needs those things now, plan around that; if it's a frontend site or prototype, it's a fast, honest way to get real code out quickly.

FAQ

Is AI website builder output actually code, or just a fancy template?

For Kodely specifically, it's real code: an actual Vite + React 19 + TypeScript + Tailwind CSS v4 project with genuine component files, viewable in the in-app code view. That's different from traditional builders, where your design is stored as internal platform data with no equivalent source file.

Can I use my own domain with an AI website builder?

It depends on the tool. Kodely currently publishes to a free *.kodely.site subdomain only; custom domains aren't supported yet.

Do AI website builders support e-commerce and backends?

Not universally, and not with Kodely today — it generates frontend-only sites with no backend, database, auth, or payments. Traditional builders with mature app ecosystems are currently the stronger choice for full e-commerce.

Is editing with an AI builder harder to learn than a drag-and-drop editor?

Usually the opposite for a first draft, since describing what you want in a sentence has a lower starting barrier than learning a block editor's layout rules. Fine-grained pixel control is where drag-and-drop editors still have an edge, because AI editing today is chat-based, not click-to-edit.

Can I try an AI website builder for free?

With Kodely, yes — sign up and get 750 free credits, no credit card required, to generate and publish a real site.
